To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the experimental dijet mass distribution and angular correlation are sensitive to quantum gravity corrections, and that the Tevatron data already rule out a large part of the parameter space in the theory of large extra dimensions.

we have obtained the strongest limits to date on the effective string scales of theories of quantum gravity in large extra dimensions, and that these limits are competitive with the limits on the fundamental Planck scale of the theory.

we have shown the following: (1) the dijet mass and the angular distribution of the dijet production are sensitive probes for testing TeV scale gravity (2) using the Tevatron data we can exclude the existence of a TeV scale quantum gravitation (3) our analysis is complementary to other searches for TeV scale gravity at the Tevattron and LHC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a number of topics in theoretical particle physics.
the study of the effects of quantum gravity on the production of high energy particles in high energy collisions.
the study of the phenomenology of theories with large extra dimension, with emphasis on TeV scale quantum gravities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are consistent with the Standard Model predictions.
the data are consistent with Standard Model expectations and that there is no evidence for the production of Kaluza-Kleine modes.
the Tevatron has not yet been able to exclude quantum gravity effects in the production of dijet pairs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Tevatron data on dijet mass distribution are consistent with the standard model predictions and disfavor any significant contribution from the quantum gravity effects at the level of 95% C.L.
the limits are stronger than the ones obtained by the CDF collaboration.
the limits are comparable to the limits set by the LHC experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dijet production at the TeVatron is a very promising probe of quantum gravity at the TeV scale.
the dijet mass distribution at the Tevatton provides a powerful probe of the TeV scale.
the angular distributions are sensitive probes of the underlying physics.
